points: Gideon and the three hundred pass over Jordan, faint, yet pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna the kings of Midian. He asks the men of Succoth for loaves of bread for his men, and the princes of Succoth answer, are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in thine hand, that we should give bread unto thine army? They try to play neutral ground for fear the kings might come against them if they helped.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: Gideon promises Succoth that when the Lord has delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into his hand, he will tear their flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with briers; and when the men of Penuel answer him the same way, he promises to break down their tower when he comes again in peace.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor with about fifteen thousand men, all that were left of the host of the children of the east, for there fell an hundred and twenty thousand men that drew sword. Three hundred against those numbers: you know God was with them.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: Returning from battle, Gideon caught a young man of Succoth who described unto him the princes and elders of the city, and he came back to Succoth with Zebah and Zalmunna in hand: behold the kings with whom ye did upbraid me. Gideon and his men had finished off Midian on an empty stomach because of them.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: Zebah and Zalmunna describe the men they slew at Tabor: each one resembled the children of a king. Those were powerful men, and they were Gideon's brethren, the sons of his mother; as the Lord liveth, if ye had saved them alive, I would not slay you.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: Zebah and Zalmunna say, rise thou, and fall upon us: for as the man is, so is his strength. They wanted to die quick at the hand of a warrior rather than suffer under the sword of a boy; so Gideon arose and slew them, and took away the ornaments that were on their camels' necks.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal
